q: When we were finally home he still cried and cried and cried.
cx: First-time mother, 2.5 months on, recalling the first weeks home after a long induction.

q: I see mother's everywhere with their strollers and their quiet, sleeping babies. Having picnics, shopping, or sitting at cafes. God I was so jealous. And its not like these babies were that much older!
cx: Her first outings with a baby who cried whenever they left the house.

q: It was so tough and makes you feel so isolated. Like you're doing something wrong or there is some secret knowledge everyone has that you don't.
cx: How the early weeks with a crying baby felt.

q: I was so scared and disappointed that I needed to be induced and declined induction from 39 weeks until 41 weeks
cx: First-time mother writing a positive induction story for others afraid of one.

q: My husband and sister were both there to support me, and they were so incredible. Lots of massaging, reminding me to drink and relax between contractions, encouraging me throughout.
cx: Who supported her in labour and how.

q: I used the TENS, and you couldn't have paid me to take it off! I know some women find it useless but I couldn't have laboured without it.
cx: The labour tool she credits most.

q: after a terrible pregnancy that made me feel like everything was doom and gloom, I actually think that the labour and birth was the best part about pregnancy overall! I felt powerful, I felt loved, and I finally met my little bub 🩷
cx: How the birth felt after a hard pregnancy.

q: I just want to shout from the rooftops how amazing my birth doula was and I think every woman should have one. If you’re currently thinking about hiring a doula do and if you’re not still do. They are 100% worth the money.
cx: A mother's unprompted verdict on her birth doula.

q: I met some angel midwives during this course and I genuinely felt however stretched they are in triage and NHS, they were doing their best to ensure a panicky mum be reassured and solaced!
cx: UK first-time mother after a heavily monitored pregnancy, on NHS midwives.

q: I saw some 7 women getting moved to labour ward before me, I felt like a failure at that point.
cx: Days on the antenatal ward waiting while an induction didn't progress.

q: I've had a super rough pregnancy and hated every second but I'm proud to announce little man arrived on Wednesday and I finally understand all the "it was worth it " posts.
cx: First-time mother days after the birth, having disliked pregnancy.

q: I'm the most sore and tired I've ever been in my life but also the most happiest.
cx: Her first days after the birth.

q: No matter how much you hated being pregnant,you're gonna love the new born euphoria.
cx: Her message to women struggling with pregnancy.

q: After 9 months of daily reddit searches "is this normal" "what do I do" "is this a sign of early labor," I went into labor at 39+6
cx: Opening of her birth story; what pregnancy looked like online.

q: It did not go according to my plan/goals whatsoever, but I have zero regrets or birth trauma. I am so proud of myself for asking questions, delaying decisions until I was ready, and trusting my team but also trusting my intuition!
cx: After a long labour with several interventions she accepted one by one.

q: The book Natural Hospital Birth ended up being SUCH a good resource and I'm glad I read it! I think it helped a ton with my confidence advocating for myself and feeling good about my choices.
cx: The preparation she credits afterwards.

q: I wish I'd done more perineal massage or went to a pelvic floor therapist regularly. It was something I'd thought about but never actually did
cx: What she wishes she had done before the birth.

q: I felt shy/awkward about it but I asked for video/pictures of him coming out, and one of the nurses did it! I love that I have those to look at now, and it makes the experience feel real instead of a fever dream.
cx: A small request in labour she is glad she made.

q: I made sure to carry one small bag that had essentials for birth (birth plan, important contacts written out, hair comb and essential oil for labor pain relief, and a huge water bottle with iced cold water to drink, a lip balm.
cx: First-time mother's birth story; what she carried in.

q: I was shocked they asked SO MANY QUESTIONS about preferences, my information, my learning styles, what are my choices for pediatricians, breastfeeding, etc. that lasted so long and it was so hard to answer during contractions
cx: Hospital admission questions during active labour.

q: Also… I didn’t use half of whatever I put in my hospital bag cuz they provide many things and I am just not in the right mind to search through bags lol
cx: What happened to her packed hospital bag.

q: ask questions when you don’t fully understand what nurse is asking or suggesting and don’t rush into a decision if you aren’t sure.
cx: Her first piece of advice after the birth.

q: Labor contraction comb to distract during contractions was so worth it for me! Get something to distract you during contractions if possible.
cx: The small tool she rated during labour.

q: No perineal massage no hypnobirth.
cx: Asked what preparation she did; contrary to course-led preparation.

q: I saw a few of these posts when I was pregnant & couldn’t wait to be on the other side. They helped reassure me so I hope I can also share that with someone else.
cx: Seven hours after her first birth, why she is posting.

q: I don’t claim that’s right for everyone but it was the decision my husband and I came to peace with.
cx: On choosing a planned surgical birth with her husband.

q: Literally nothing went to plan and I had to accept most things I specifically didn't want
cx: Right after the birth; she still felt it was worth it.

q: I'm thankful I had this sub to check in with and read similar experiences/questions I had over the course of these last 40 weeks
cx: What helped her through the pregnancy.

q: Funny enough he was NOWHERE to be seen in the entire process 😭
cx: Her doctor, who chose the induction, was absent during labour.
